output.reason: Reported itchy blistering rash limited to both forearms after a named poison ivy exposure while clearing brush, with fever and breathing trouble denied; the described spread is within the same forearm area and typical of delayed contact dermatitis. No decision-critical need for clinician assessment, prescribing or testing is established on the reported facts, so guidance with a symptom-specific safety net is sufficient.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now with over-the-counter itch relief; ask your pharmacist what suits you. What you describe — itchy blisters on both forearms after brush clearing, no fever and no breathing trouble — fits a typical poison ivy reaction, and apparent spread within that area is common. If the rash becomes painful, warm or pus-filled, spreads to your face or genitals, or you develop fever, arrange a same-day clinician assessment (Counsel messaging or an in-person urgent service). If you get trouble breathing or throat/facial swelling, call 911.
